messages.subject: Joint disease mapping
parts:
Dear all

Spatial Models with the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation within Markov Chain Monte Carlo Virgilio G´omez-Rubioa, ∗ , Francisco Palm´ı-Perales a

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Joint disease mapping
parts:
Hi,

Sorry I forgot to reply to all...

I have a problem to get the INLA syntax for modeling joint disease. There is an article 
Spatial Models with the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation within Markov Chain Monte Carlo Virgilio G´omez-Rubioa, ∗ , Francisco Palm´ı-Perales a

That paper is an application to spatial models of this more general paper:

https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07844
However I have a problem how to run joint disease mapping in INLA using share component approach.

The code to fit that models for a fixed set of parameters (m.delta) is below. We are using a model with 3 likelihoods for this. However, the model requires MCMC on the spatial weights, and unless you have a large dataset the model will run faster with jags or WinBUGS.

Right now I cannot give you a reproducible example because our data is confidential, but if you can find a publicly available dataset with three or more diseases (observed, expected and boundaries of areas) I'll be happy to share this.

If you have two diseases you can use the besag2 latent model to fit a similar model, I think.

Best,

Virgilio

---

fit.inla <- function(data, m.delta) {
  data$delta <- m.delta[data$r]
  form.joint <- OBS ~ -1 + rf +
    f(AREAID, model = "besag", graph = W, replicate = r,
      hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(0.01, 0.01)))) +
    f(AREAID.com, delta, model = "besag", graph = W,
      hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(0.01, 0.01))))

  res <- inla(form.joint, data = data, family = rep("poisson", 3), E = data$EXP)

  #???We need to change mlik to account for m.delta
  #res$mlik <- res$mlik - 47*sum(log(m.delta))

  return(list(mlik = res$mlik[1,1], model = res))

}
